item.title: Police seeking help in identifying woman's body found at Thurston Garden last Friday
item.description: Following the discovery of a woman’s body at Thurston Garden in Suva on Friday night, police are seeking public assistance to identify her. They say the woman is believed to be iTaukei and aged between 30 to 40 years old.
item.content:encoded:
Following the discovery of a woman’s body at Thurston Garden in Suva on Friday night, police are seeking public assistance to identify her.

They say the woman is believed to be iTaukei and aged between 30 to 40 years old.

She is about 160 centimetres tall, with a brown complexion and black hair with burgundy dye on top.

She also has a tattoo of the word “Kadavu” on her right shoulder, with a leaf underneath it.

With this being the third body found since last week.

Anyone with information is urged to contact Crime Stoppers on 919 or the Fiji Police Call Centre on 1681.

Meanwhile, the body of a man was retrieved from the Labasa River.

fijivillage News has received confirmation that the victim is former soccer player Nemani Rasiga.

In a separate case in the Western Division, a woman was found lying motionless near a complex in Nadi last week Thursday.

Her body was recovered and taken to the Nadi Hospital mortuary, where a post-mortem examination will be conducted to establish the cause of death.

Police say investigations into the Labasa and Nadi cases are continuing, and anyone with information that could assist investigators is urged to call 1681.

item.content:encoded:
Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa will appear on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 7pm Wednesday.

The show will focus on the state of preparedness of the Fijian Elections Office for the proposed national referendum on December 9th and the next general elections which has to be held by February 6th 2027, the nationwide voter registration underway, changes to the electoral laws and the impact on the voters and the country, and the impact of any drastic changes with two months to go for the last day for the Writ of Elections to be issued on December 24th 2026 amongst other issues.

You can watch the Straight Talk interview on our facebook page, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram accounts.

You can also check out the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple podcasts.

item.title: Former Lautoka Mayor calls for protection of iTaukei rights while supporting recognition of Fiji as a Christian State
item.description: Former Lautoka Mayor Kenneth Low has called for the protection of iTaukei rights, culture and traditions in the Constitution and has also expressed his support for recognising Fiji as a Christian State. During consultations on proposed constitutional amendments, Low says his family has lived in Fiji for four generations, and he believes the Constitution must safeguard the interests of indigenous F
item.content:encoded:
Former Lautoka Mayor Kenneth Low has called for the protection of iTaukei rights, culture and traditions in the Constitution and has also expressed his support for recognising Fiji as a Christian State.

During consultations on proposed constitutional amendments, Low says his family has lived in Fiji for four generations, and he believes the Constitution must safeguard the interests of indigenous Fijians for future generations.

Low says he fully supports the Great Council of Chiefs and believes there is nothing wrong with recognising Fiji as a Christian State because, Fiji's identity is closely linked to the culture, traditions and values of its indigenous people.

He raised concerns about immigration and citizenship, saying the indigenous Fijian population is relatively small and constitutional safeguards are needed to protect their culture, rights and interests as the country's population changes.

Low also expressed support for the government's decision to amend the 2013 Constitution rather than replacing it entirely.

He acknowledged that constitutional reform involves political considerations and differing views however, he says developing a Constitution that will serve future generations should take priority over political considerations, including the timing of the next general election.

Low says the government and the committee should take additional time if necessary to ensure Fiji has a Constitution that will benefit future generations.

He says there are people accusing the government for delaying the elections or possibly trying to get more money stating that is just rubbish talk.

He adds the contributions of Indo-Fijians to the country's development should be recognised alongside the interests of indigenous landowners.

Low says landowners should be given greater opportunities and support to benefit from their land.

He has also called for an increase in the retirement age of judges, saying older professionals still have valuable experience and knowledge to contribute.

Low also raised concerns about corruption, drug-related activities and law enforcement, questioning whether authorities are doing enough to address these issues.

item.title: Jobs expected as RB Patel invests $25M in new 7-storey, 21-apartment complex in Suva
item.description: RB Patel is investing $25 million in a seven-storey, 21-apartment complex in Suva as it expands its property portfolio, with the project expected to create employment and business opportunities while keeping investment benefits within Fiji. The proposed apartment complex will be built at 25 Knolly Street and will include two levels of car parking and 21 two- to three-bedroom apartments.
item.content:encoded:
RB Patel is investing $25 million in a seven-storey, 21-apartment complex in Suva as it expands its property portfolio, with the project expected to create employment and business opportunities while keeping investment benefits within Fiji.

The proposed apartment complex will be built at 25 Knolly Street and will include two levels of car parking and 21 two- to three-bedroom apartments.

Minister for iTaukei Affairs Ifereimi Vasu says the project will take about 15 months to complete and is expected to create jobs.

Vasu says further employment and business opportunities are expected once the complex is completed, although the number of jobs has not been specified.

The project will be constructed by Global Construct PTE Limited, a Chinese company undertaking its first project in Fiji.

Vasu says RB Patel has continued to invest in property development alongside its supermarket, wholesale and distribution businesses.

The company operates 12 supermarkets across Fiji and has a property portfolio worth more than $80 million as of 30 June this year.

Its existing developments include Checkpoint Complex in Martintar, Nadi, Harbour Point Complex and a convention centre in Lami, as well as residential apartments in Clark Street, Suva.

RB Patel is also developing a $20 million commercial complex on a 10-acre site in Wailevu, Macuata, which is expected to be completed around June to July next year.

The company has also identified future development opportunities in Ba, Nadawa and Suva.

Fijian Holdings Limited Group CEO Jaoji Koroi says RB Patel is one of FHL's key subsidiaries, with FHL acquiring a majority stake in the company in 2007.

Koroi says more than 90 percent of RB Patel's shareholder base comprises major local institutions, including the iTaukei Trust Fund, BSP Life and the Fiji National Provident Fund.

He says this means the benefits generated through the company's investments can remain in Fiji and support local communities.

Koroi says FHL Group's total assets exceeded $1 billion for the first time this year, following $436 million in investments across various sectors over the past four years.

He says FHL recorded a consolidated group profit of $67 million for the financial year ending June 2026.

Meanwhile, Vasu says Government recognises that economic development is important to the social and economic well-being of the people.

He says successful development requires cooperation between landowners, traditional institutions, statutory bodies, investors, financial institutions and the private sector.

RB Patel Chairman Jitoko Tikolevu says the company aims to strengthen its property investments, provide spaces for businesses and services, and support economic activity across Fiji.

item.title: Water shortage hits Viwa Island as district nurse raises concerns over children's health
item.description: 61-year-old Venina Kula of Naibalebale Village says finding water has become one of the biggest challenges for families, who are searching for enough to drink, prepare meals and wash clothes. She says the shortage has been particularly been difficult for mothers trying to meet their children's daily needs.
item.content:encoded:
61-year-old Venina Kula of Naibalebale Village says finding water has become one of the biggest challenges for families, who are searching for enough to drink, prepare meals and wash clothes.

She says the shortage has been particularly been difficult for mothers trying to meet their children's daily needs.

District Nurse Iliesa Ratuva says limited access to clean water is also affecting his ability to care for patients.

He believes the shortage has contributed to cases of skin infections, scabies and diarrhoea, particularly among children.

Ratuva is also concerned about dehydration and the risk of illness if stored water becomes contaminated.

According to the Water Authority of Fiji, Viwa Island has three villages and relies entirely on rainwater, leaving families vulnerable during prolonged periods without rain.

The Authority says emergency water supplies have now been delivered to affected communities and essential facilities as part of the Government's response to the dry conditions.

Water has been delivered to Viwa District School and its quarters, Viwa Nursing Station, Viwa Village and Yalobi Nursing Station.

Kula says the delivery has brought much-needed relief and peace of mind to families, particularly mothers who have been worried about providing enough water for their children.

Ratuva says the clean water will help residents maintain hygiene, prepare meals and reduce the risk of water-related illnesses.

The emergency delivery was coordinated by the Ministry of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport through Government Shipping Services, in partnership with the Water Authority of Fiji and other Government agencies.

The Water Authority of Fiji says emergency water deliveries will continue to vulnerable maritime communities affected by the prolonged dry weather.

item.title: Riyaz and Sagar acquitted in Volkswagen tender and procurement case
item.description: Former Fijian Broadcasting Corporation CEO Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and current Chief Financial Officer Vimlesh Sagar have been acquitted in the $207,470 Volkswagen tender and procurement case after FICAC confirmed the withdrawal of charges. This is the same matter in which Sayed-Khaiyum and Sagar were re-charged following the discontinuation of the case in May last year.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fijian Broadcasting Corporation CEO Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and current Chief Financial Officer Vimlesh Sagar have been acquitted in the $207,470 Volkswagen tender and procurement case after FICAC confirmed the withdrawal of charges.

This is the same matter in which Sayed-Khaiyum and Sagar were re-charged following the discontinuation of the case in May last year.

FICAC says they could not meet element of the offence.

Magistrate Joseph Daurewa informed Sayed-Khaiyum and Sagar that they had been acquitted after the charges were withdrawn.

Magistrate Daurewa also discharged all bail conditions imposed on both men.

Speaking to the media outside the court, Sayed-Khaiyum said this was the second time they had been charged in the case, describing it as a conspiracy.

He alleges he had been targeted and had been unable to secure employment since he was charged.

Sayed-Khaiyum says that, having worked in the media industry for almost 30 years, he had demonstrated the utmost honesty and integrity.

He further says he had not misused a single dollar.

When asked whether he would enter politics, Sayed-Khaiyum said no.

Meanwhile, Sagar said many questions had been raised about his character and that the case had been difficult for him and his family.

He says all audits dating back to 2023 were clear.

Sagar adds that the case had tarnished his reputation.

He thanked those who had stood by him throughout the case.

Sayed-Khaiyum was charged with one count of abuse of office for gain and one count of general dishonesty causing a loss.

Sayed-Khaiyum and Sagar had both pleaded not guilty to charges relating to the tender and procurement of a 3.0-litre Volkswagen Touareg valued at $207,470.
